title: Minimal Aligned Power-of-Two Range Blocks
description: An aligned power-of-two block (like a CIDR IP block or binary buddy-allocator block) is a contiguous integer interval `[a, a + 2^k - 1]` of length `2^k` (`k >= 0`) whose starting address `a` is divisible by `2^k`. Given a non-negative starting integer `start` and a positive integer length `n`, return the minimum number of disjoint aligned power-of-two blocks required to exactly cover the interval `[start, start + n - 1]`.
hints: At the current position `start`, the largest aligned block starting at `start` has size limited by `lowbit(start) = start & -start` (using two's complement; unbounded when `start == 0`).
The block size also cannot exceed the highest power of two `<= n`. Repeatedly advance `start += step` and `n -= step` with `step = min(lowbit(start), highestPow2(n))` until `n == 0`.

examples.explanation: Interval [0, 7] is itself a single aligned block of length 8.
Interval [1, 6] splits into 4 aligned blocks: [1,1], [2,3], [4,5], and [6,6].
Interval [4, 10] splits into 3 aligned blocks: [4,7], [8,9], and [10,10].
